name: Ahura Mazda
role: Supreme god, the Wise Lord, creator and source of asha
fun_fact: Zoroastrians honour Ahura Mazda through fire, but the fire is a symbol and focus of purity rather than the god himself.

name: Angra Mainyu
role: The destructive spirit, adversary of Ahura Mazda and source of druj
fun_fact: In the Gathas Angra Mainyu is the evil spirit who chose destruction; the later Bundahishn calls him Ahriman and makes him the leader of a host of demons.

name: Yima
role: Early king and culture hero, called Jamshid in later Persian tradition
fun_fact: Yima is remembered both as a king who made the world flourish and, in later legend, as a ruler whose pride cost him his royal glory.

name: Zarathushtra
role: Prophet and poet, the founding voice of the Gathas
fun_fact: His Greek name Zoroaster gave the religion its English name, and his hymns are still recited in Zoroastrian ritual today.

name: Kaveh
role: Blacksmith who raises the people against Zahhak
fun_fact: Kaveh's apron became the Derafsh Kaviani, the royal standard of Iran, and his name remains a byword for resistance to tyranny in Persian tradition.

name: Zahhak
role: Tyrannical king with two serpents on his shoulders
fun_fact: Zahhak grows from an older Avestan dragon, Azi Dahaka, into a human king in the Shahnameh, showing how epic poetry reshaped ancient myth.

name: Rostam
role: Greatest hero of the Shahnameh, prince of Sistan
fun_fact: Rostam's seven trials are called the Haft Khan, and his horse Rakhsh is as famous in Persian art as the hero himself.

name: Rakhsh
role: Rostam's stallion and companion in battle
fun_fact: Rakhsh is no ordinary mount: he fights beside Rostam, warns him of danger, and shares the hardship of the seven trials.

name: Zal
role: White-haired hero and father of Rostam
fun_fact: Zal's white hair, once taken as a bad omen, became a mark of his special place among heroes.

name: Simurgh
role: Great benevolent bird of Iranian myth
fun_fact: The Simurgh is far older than the Shahnameh: a bird called Saena appears in the Avesta, and the epic makes her the protector of Zal and his family.
